What the model says when you point its attention somewhere

Hover a region of the scan. The model was never told where to look in words — its gaze heads were steered onto that region and it was asked the same question every time. Nothing was retrained. The radiologist's box is shown only to check the answer, never given to the model.

Cases — SLAKE, open access

How to read this

These answers are precomputed on the cluster, not generated live in your browser. Every region of every case was decoded ahead of time so the page can be static.

The nine tiles under the scan are the model's log-probability for the radiologist's own phrase when steered to each region. The tile with a green underline is the region that actually contains the radiologist's box. When the highest tile is that tile, the model localised the finding without ever being told where it was.

Steering strength matters, and past a point it breaks the model. Localisation stops improving around 8, but text quality keeps falling: at 16 and above roughly a third of generations collapse into repetition. The setting inherited from prior work is 10,000, which is far past that. Move the control to 16 or 64 to see it happen.

Scans are from SLAKE (Liu et al., 2021), used here with attribution; see the repository for licence details. The chest X-ray corpora in this study — MS-CXR, VinDr-CXR and Chest ImaGenome — are PhysioNet credentialed data and are deliberately absent from this page.
